cls: Antineoplastic - anti-VEGF recombinant monoclonal antibody (angiogenesis inhibitor)
pharm: Binds and neutralises vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF-A), preventing its interaction with VEGFR-1/2 on endothelial cells and thereby inhibiting tumour angiogenesis and vascular permeability
quick: 5-15 mg/kg IV every 2-3 weeks depending on tumour and regimen
Can cause fetal harm; use contraception during and 6 months after
Do not breastfeed during and for 6 months after the last dose
No specific dose adjustment; monitor proteinuria
BP, urine protein, bleeding, GI symptoms, wound healing
summary: Bevacizumab is an intravenous recombinant humanised anti-VEGF monoclonal antibody (angiogenesis inhibitor) used, usually with chemotherapy, for metastatic colorectal cancer, non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer, recurrent glioblastoma, metastatic renal cell carcinoma, cervical, ovarian/fallopian/peritoneal and hepatocellular cancers. Doses range from 5 to 15 mg/kg IV every 2-3 weeks depending on tumour and regimen. It carries BOXED-level warnings for gastrointestinal perforation and fistulae, surgery and wound-healing complications (withhold at least 28 days before and after major surgery), and severe or fatal haemorrhage - do not give within 28 days of major surgery or in the setting of recent haemoptysis. Other serious effects include hypertension, thromboembolism, proteinuria/nephrotic syndrome and posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome.
indications: Metastatic colorectal cancer (first- or second-line, with fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy)
First-line unresectable, locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (with carboplatin/paclitaxel)
Metastatic renal cell carcinoma (with interferon alfa)
Persistent, recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer (with chemotherapy)
Epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer (various settings)

dosage.d: 5 mg/kg every 2 weeks with bolus-IFL, or 10 mg/kg every 2 weeks with FOLFOX4; 5 mg/kg q2w or 7.5 mg/kg q3w after progression
15 mg/kg every 3 weeks with carboplatin and paclitaxel
First infusion over 90 minutes; if tolerated, second over 60 minutes and subsequent over 30 minutes
dosage.n: Do not give as IV push or bolus

admin: Administer by intravenous infusion only - never as an IV push or bolus
Give the first infusion over 90 minutes; if well tolerated, the second over 60 minutes and subsequent infusions over 30 minutes
Withhold for at least 28 days before elective surgery and do not give for at least 28 days after major surgery and until the wound has adequately healed
Do not initiate in patients with recent haemoptysis (>=2.5 mL of red blood)
Monitor blood pressure every 2-3 weeks and urine protein during therapy

Discontinue permanently for GI perforation, fistula involving an internal organ, serious haemorrhage, severe arterial thromboembolism, hypertensive crisis/encephalopathy, PRES, nephrotic syndrome or wound dehiscence requiring intervention
moa: Bevacizumab is a recombinant humanised IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF-A) and prevents it from interacting with its receptors (VEGFR-1 and VEGFR-2) on the surface of endothelial cells. VEGF is a key mediator of tumour angiogenesis; neutralising it reduces microvascular growth, regresses existing tumour vasculature and decreases vascular permeability, thereby inhibiting tumour growth and metastasis. The same anti-angiogenic action impairs physiological vascular repair, explaining bleeding, wound-healing, perforation and thrombotic toxicities.

absolute: There are no listed absolute contraindications in the US label; bevacizumab should not be initiated for 28 days after major surgery or in the presence of recent serious haemorrhage/haemoptysis
relative: Recent major surgery or non-healed surgical wound
Recent haemoptysis or active serious bleeding
monitor: Signs of GI perforation or fistula (abdominal pain, fever)

preg: Based on its mechanism (inhibition of angiogenesis) and animal data, bevacizumab can cause fetal harm, including embryo-fetal malformations and reduced fetal weight. Advise of the risk and ensure effective contraception in females of reproductive potential during treatment and for 6 months after the last dose.
lact: There are no data on the presence of bevacizumab in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant and the long half-life, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 6 months after the last dose.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is provided for renal impairment. Bevacizumab can cause proteinuria and, rarely, nephrotic syndrome and thrombotic microangiopathy; monitor urine protein and withhold for >=2 g/24 h proteinuria until it falls below this level, and discontinue for nephrotic syndrome.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is provided for hepatic impairment.

major: Sunitinib - concurrent use has caused microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia; avoid combination
Anthracycline-based chemotherapy / prior anthracycline or chest irradiation - increased risk of congestive heart failure
moderate: Anticoagulants and antiplatelet agents - increased bleeding risk; weigh carefully
Concurrent chemotherapy - additive toxicities (e.g. neutropenia, GI effects)
minor: No clinically significant CYP-mediated metabolic interactions (monoclonal antibody)
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor blood pressure and urine protein; bevacizumab can interfere with wound healing and surgical planning

serious: Severe or fatal haemorrhage (pulmonary, GI, CNS)
Surgery and wound-healing complications, including dehiscence and necrotising fasciitis
Severe hypertension / hypertensive crisis and hypertensive encephalopathy
Nephrotic syndrome and renal injury / thrombotic microangiopathy
emergency: Major haemorrhage (haemoptysis, GI or intracranial bleeding)

monitoring: Blood pressure every 2-3 weeks during therapy
Signs of bleeding, GI perforation or fistula
Wound healing around any surgical procedure
Cardiac function in patients with prior anthracyclines or chest irradiation
counsel: Tell your team about any planned surgery or dental work - this drug must be paused around operations to allow wound healing
Report severe abdominal pain, fever, vomiting or constipation (possible bowel perforation)
Report any unusual bleeding - coughing or vomiting blood, blood in stool, severe nosebleeds, or sudden severe headache
Your blood pressure and urine will be checked regularly
Report new weakness, vision changes, severe headache, seizures or confusion (PRES)
Use effective contraception during and for 6 months after treatment and do not breastfeed during this period
pk: Pharmacodynamic anti-angiogenic effect develops over the dosing cycle
Predictable, dose-proportional serum concentrations after IV infusion
Terminal elimination half-life approximately 20 days (range ~11-50 days)
Effects and bleeding/wound-healing risk persist for weeks given the long half-life
Refrigerate vials at 2-8 C, protect from light, do not freeze or shake; diluted infusion stored per label
pearls: BOXED-level warnings: GI perforation, surgery/wound-healing complications, and severe/fatal haemorrhage
Withhold >=28 days before elective surgery and at least 28 days after major surgery until the wound heals
Do not initiate with recent haemoptysis; avoid in squamous NSCLC due to pulmonary haemorrhage risk
Monitor blood pressure and urine protein routinely; withhold for proteinuria >=2 g/24 h, stop for nephrotic syndrome
Watch for arterial/venous thromboembolism and PRES
Long half-life (~20 days) - effects persist well after the last dose
missed: Bevacizumab is given by a healthcare professional every 2-3 weeks. If an infusion is missed, contact the oncology team to reschedule; doses are not made up at home.
overdose: The highest tested dose was associated with severe migraine. There is no specific antidote for overdose; manage supportively and monitor for the known toxicities (hypertension, bleeding, thromboembolism, proteinuria).
